whatItIs.text: The sweet, heat-free fruit of Capsicum annuum, sold green, yellow, orange or red; red bells are simply ripened green ones, so they taste the sweetest.

historyNote.text: Peppers are native to the Americas — the genus probably originated in Bolivia and Brazil and was domesticated in Mesoamerica — and seeds reached Spain by 1493; cave finds suggest people were eating peppers some 7,000 years ago.

howToChoose.text: Choose heavy, glossy peppers with taut skin and a fresh-looking green stem end; wrinkled or soft ones have started drying out.

storage.text: Store loosely wrapped in the fridge crisper and keep dry. The rulebook has the shelf-life guidance.
storage.note: shelf-life guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Blister peppers under the grill, peel if you like, and dress the strips with oil and vinegar for sandwiches or antipasti.

substitutions.note: in cooked dishes, for similar colour and water content; less sweetness
